claims.location: source name, characteristics[treatment], characteristics[expression system], characteristics[protein preparation], comment[data file] rows 1-7
claims.value: Six purified GST-BUGZ runs (three DMSO, three PTL) and one HeLa GFP-BUGZ run
claims.evidence: Exact RAW filenames identify GST-BugZ and DMSO/PTL, or WT1_SDS; paper Methods describes recombinant GST-BUGZ from E. coli Rosetta2 and GFP-BUGZ HeLa pulldown. WT1 treatment is not available.

claims.value: E. coli expression host for purified GST-BUGZ; human HeLa for GFP-BUGZ pulldown
claims.evidence: Paper Methods explicitly states GST-BUGZ purification from Rosetta2 bacteria and GFP-BUGZ from HeLa cells. The human BUGZ protein sequence origin is distinct from bacterial expression host.

claims.value: impact II for six GST runs; timsTOF Pro for WT1
claims.evidence: PRIDE lists impact II and timsTOF Pro. HTTP-range central directories of all seven accession-specific RAW ZIPs show analysis.baf plus microTOFQImpactAcquisition.method for every GST run, and analysis.tdf plus ddaPASEF method for WT1.

claims.location: comment[proteomics data acquisition method], comment[cleavage agent details] rows 1-7
claims.evidence: Paper and PRIDE sample protocol state DDA operation and overnight trypsin digestion of BUGZ preparations.

limitations: The seven archive indexes establish instrument format but do not expose full scan settings; dissociation and mass tolerances are omitted.
The publication describes GFP-BUGZ pulldown from PTL-treated HeLa cells, but the WT1_SDS RAW filename does not encode whether that run received PTL; treatment is not available for that row.
GST-BUGZ is a recombinant human protein expressed in E. coli; organism records expression host for the purified sample, while protein sequence origin is human.
Biological replicate 1 is a required coordinate for each uniquely named purified preparation, not an assertion that the six preparations are independent biological replicates.
Generic PRIDE reconciliation inspects only one instrument and flags Impact II against timsTOF Pro despite both being listed in the record and mapped to separate RAW archives.
